title.narrative: Project for Strengthening Public Financial Management

description.narrative: The objective of the Strengthening Public Financial Management Project for Micronesia is to improve tax administration and the completeness, reliability and timeliness of financial reports of the National and State Governments. The project has 5 components. 1. Strengthening the public financial management environment component will strengthen the Public Financial Management (PFM) environment by ensuring that the legal and regulatory framework and the procedural guidance for business processes governing budget formulation, budget execution, and financial reporting for revenues and expenditures are internally consistent, aligned with the applicable accounting guidance, and streamlined for efficiency. The scope will include all five governments, each of which has its own set of regulations and procedures. 2. Financial management information system component will implement a new Financial Management Information System that will support effective management of public resources and improve financial reporting for management and accountability. 3. Revenue Management System (RMS) component will improve the efficiency and effectiveness of revenue management for the National Government of the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM). 4. Change management and human resource development component will successful implementation of the FMIS and the RMS with active stakeholder engagement and development of individual competencies and institutional capacity needed to sustain FMIS and RMS operations and related PFM functions. The project will support capacity building in the Department of Finance and Administration (DoFA) and other agencies with key roles in the PFM cycle such as the Office of the National Public Auditor. 5. Project management component will support overall project management and coordination.
The objective of the project is to improve tax administration and the completeness, reliability and timeliness of financial reports of the National and State Governments.

condition.narrative: Centralized Implementation UnitSection I.A.6 of Schedule 26. The Recipient shall maintain until the Closing Date the CentralImplementation Unit with mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall be responsible forproviding fiduciary, monitoring and coordination of development partner funded projects. Without limitation to the generality ofthe foregoing, the Central Implementation Unit shall include staff performing the following key functions, each with terms ofreference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association: (a) program management; (b) procurement; (c) safeguards;(d) communications; (e) monitoring and evaluation; and (f) financial management.

Dated CovenantsMid-term ReviewSection II.2 of Schedule 2The Recipient shall: (a) not later than January 31, 2021 (or suchother date as the Association may agree in writing), prepare and furnish to the Association a mid-term report, in such detail asthe Association shall reasonably request, documenting progress achieved in the carrying out of the Project during the periodpreceding the date of such report, taking into account the monitoring and evaluation activities performed pursuant to paragraph 1of this Section II, and setting out the measures recommended to ensure the continued efficient carrying out of the Project and theachievement of its objective during the period following such date; and (b) review with the Association such mid-term report, on orabout the date one month after its submission, carry out a mid-term review of the Project, and thereafter take all measuresrequired to ensure the continued efficient implementation of the Project and the achievement of its objectives, based on theconclusions and recommendations of the mid-term report and the Association's views on the matter.

Intergovernmental PFM Working GroupSection I.A.4 of Schedule 2To this end, the Recipient shall establish, by no later thanthree (3) months after the Effective Date, and maintain until the Closing Date, the Intergovernmental PFM Working Group, chaired bythe Assistant Secretary of Treasury (or such other person which the Association has confirmed in writing to the Recipient asacceptable to the Association), and comprised of members of the respective Technical Working Groups and other technical leads from,inter alia, the offices of the National Government and State Governments with finance, budget and information technology functions,and with an institutional framework, functions, and resources satisfactory to the Association as shall be required for the Project.

Project Steering CommitteeSection I.A.2 of Schedule 2To this end, the Recipient shall maintain until the Closing Date, theProject Steering Committee, chaired by its Secretary of Finance (or such other person which the Association has confirmed inwriting to the Recipient as acceptable to the Association), and comprised of the directors, or their representatives, of each ofthe State Finance Offices, and with an institutional framework, functions, and resources satisfactory to the Association as shallbe required for the Project.

Project implementation UnitSection I.A.5 of Schedule 2The Recipient shall maintain until the Closing Date the ProjectImplementation Unit within the National Department of Finance and Administration with mandate, composition and resourcessatisfactory to the Association, which shall be responsible for providing day to day management of Project implementation. Withoutlimitation to the generality of the foregoing, the Project Implementation Unit shall be supported by specialists within the CentralImplementation Unit, and shall include the following key staff, each with terms of reference, qualifications and experiencesatisfactory to the Association: (a) a Project manager; (b) a Project assistant; and (c) additional technical specialists as may beneeded.
The Recipient shall update, no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, and thereafter adopt, the Project ImplementationManual, in form and substance acceptable to the Association.

title.narrative: IR-9: Transparency and citizen engagement in budget preparation and execution by National government

baseline.value: DoFA website exists but does not provide platform for receiving citizen feedback.

target.value: DoFA website includes functionality to capture citizen feedback.Information on budget preparation stages, final budget and quarterly updates on budget execution posted regularly including:a) summary presented in a citizen-friendly format understandable by non-technical audience;b) summary of citizen-feedback received and government response.

comment.narrative: Website has been improved to capture feedback. The citizen-friendly budget FY2024 was published in February 2024 and FY 2025 was published in June 2025. Currently the DoFA website has no information on budget preparation stages, there are no links to the budget appropriation acts, no quarterly updates on budget execution, and no summary of citizen feedback received and the government's response. There has been no citizen feedback via the website as this was not publicized at all. Therefore no report on citizen feedback on the website will be produced. Y2 and Y3 will remain partially achieved. https://dofa.gov.fm/fmis-general-comments/ https://dofa.gov.fm/rms-general-comments/

actual.value: Yr.1 target achieved. Yr.2 and Yr.5 partially achieved.

title.narrative: PDO-1: In-year budget reports prepared and published by National and all four State governments

baseline.value: In-year budget reports not prepared and not published

target.value: In-year budget reports prepared and cleared for publication by all five Govts meeting criteria for timing, accuracy, coverage and comparability to meet criteria of “B” score for PI-28 based on PEFA Framework.

comment.narrative: Not all States/national have prepared two consecutive quarterly in-year budget reports as yet. An assessment against the criteria for PEFA PI-28 (In-year budget reports) indicates that for 28.1 (Coverage and comparability) the C score is already met, for 28.3 (Accuracy) the B score is already met, and for 28.2 (timing ) the score is currently a C. Several states are still awaiting clearance for publication apart from Yap and National.

actual.value: Yr 1 target achieved. Yr 3 –Yr 5 is partially achieved

title.narrative: PDO-3: New FMIS used by all five govts for recording and reporting budget, revenue and expenditure

baseline.value: FundWare accounting system being phased out

target.value: New FMIS used for preparation of budget for FY2024 and recording of revenue and expenditure transactions by National and all State governments

comment.narrative: Year 2-5 targets: Testing is ongoing, parallel processing planned, operational acceptance planned mid-August. Significant progress has been made towards the roll-out but these targets will not be achieved before project closure.

title.narrative: IR-4: Taxpayer accounting in Customs and Tax Administration (CTA) automated

baseline.value: No RMS in place

target.value: All modules of RMS implemented and in use

comment.narrative: All modules are now in use. The e-payment platform is not yet live, but this is part of the payment module. The e-tax and RMS portals are now live. Time slippage over course of RMS project has led to rushed implementation at the end of the project. The handover ceremony of the RMS to government took place on July 18. Some final functionality testing is still ongoing to ensure integrity of system. The e-payment function is expected to go live before project closure so will need to be assessed in August.

title.narrative: IR-8: Gender-sensitive communication conducted for the project for awareness and building ownership

baseline.value: No communication strategy; regular updates and information not released for government staff and citizens

target.value: DoFA website enhanced and regularly updated with information for government staff and citizens with functionality developed for capturing and summarizing feedback

comment.narrative: Yr.3 and Yr.5 target achieved. Yr.1 not yet achieved. Yr2 and Yr.4 partially achieved. The website also includes functionality to capture feedback from citizens through two feedback pages (one for the the FMIS and one for the RMS), although these were not publicized so no feedback has been received. Further work on two way citizen engagement will be carried forward to PFM II.

actual.value: Yr.3 and Yr.5 target achieved. Yr.1 not yet achieved. Yr2 and Yr.4 partially achieved.

title.narrative: IR-5: Competency framework specifying minimum skillsets adopted and used for all PFM related jobs

baseline.value: No competencies defined for PFM related roles

target.value: Competency framework specifying minimum skillsets required adopted for PFM related jobs across National and State governments and used for recruitment and training to build gender-balanced workforce

comment.narrative: Draft DoFA Competency Framework Policy mandates the use of the competency framework for recruitment and training. The policy doesn't apply to State level - therefore partially achieved. Yr5: If policy is in place as per the above it would be used for recruitment and training for DoFA. Partially achieved as it won't be in place in the states.

actual.value: Y1 and Yr3 target achieved. Yr. 2,4 and 5 have not yet achieved.

title.narrative: IR-6: External training program partnerships for PFM related certification and degree courses

baseline.value: No external training program partnerships in place

target.value: Four (4) external training program partnerships for certification and degree courses in PFM related disciplines

comment.narrative: Target has been met. Partnerships entered into with Alison, Career and Technical Education Center (CTEC), Charles Strurt and Cook Islands Tertiary Training Institute Partnership.

title.narrative: IR-2: Procedures Manuals updated with detailed guidance for all five governments

baseline.value: Operations Procedure not covering all required areas

target.value: Procedures Manuals in place with detailed guidance for budget formulation, accounting, internal controls, payroll, fixed assets, liabilities (including debt), cash management and financial reporting

comment.narrative: An Accounting Manual was drafted for national government in 2024 but this is still pending and won't be finalized before project closure. State Procedures Manuals have not been prepared and will not be completed before project closure. FreeBalance is working on user guides currently and these are expected to be completed before project closure. Years 2-5 targets will not be achieved and these will be will be pushed forward to Component 1 work of PFM II.

title.narrative: IR-3: Financial data integrity maintained to meet “B” score for PI-27

baseline.value: “B+” score for PI-27 in 2016 self-assessment

target.value: Criteria for "B" score for PI-27 fully met

comment.narrative: New FMIS system has been procured and includes controls for data integrity, restricted access, recording and audit trail. Assessment against PEFA PI-28 (in-year budget reports) has been completed based on current processes in Fundware given that the new FMIS is not yet live. 27.1 (bank account reconciliation) is assessed as a B, 27.2 (suspense accounts) is N/A (since there are no suspense accounts), 27.3 (advance accounts) as a D and 27.4 (financial data integrity processes) as a B. Therefore year 2 and 4 targets will remain as partially achieved at project closure. The strengthening of travel advance reconciliations will carry forward to PFM II under support provided through Component 1.
